Grip giving out before your back does is common, and it's a fixable training problem. The simplest fix is to hang from the bar for sets of 20 to 40 seconds a couple of times a week, and carry something heavy like dumbbells or a loaded bag for a minute at a time. Both build grip without taking much out of you.

On pull-up days, chalk helps a lot if your gym allows it. Keep the bar low in your fingers with your thumb wrapped around it, rather than gripping in the palm. Squeezing the bar hard before you pull also makes the whole movement feel steadier.

If the grip is the only thing stopping you, put your heavy rows and deadlifts before pull-ups so you aren't pre-fatiguing your hands. Straps are fine on a few back sets, but keep most of your pulling strap-free so the grip actually catches up.

If you want, I can add dead hangs or carries to your program.
